title: GSK drinks in Chai Discovery’s AI models after wet-lab validation
key_facts: Chai Discovery, an AI company building a computer-aided design suite for molecules, announced a collaboration with GSK.
It follows a technology evaluation in which GSK ran internal wet-lab tests of Chai's designs.
Chai generated the designs for GSK targets zero-shot, without target-specific training.
GSK found binders to all tested targets, which led to the broader collaboration.
GSK now gets access to Chai's platform, including protein folding and design models.
Chai's latest model is Chai-3; Chai says it achieves high target success rates and binding affinities.
GSK's Christopher Austin says the technology complements GSK's own internal models.
quote_evidence: The agreement follows a successful technology evaluation in which GSK conducted internal wet-lab testing of Chai’s designs.
GSK found binders to all tested targets—resulting in the expansion of its work with Chai into a broader collaboration.
We evaluated their models across a panel of diverse targets and saw designs with strong binding affinities.
why_it_matters_hint: A big drugmaker is expanding use of AI-designed molecules after its own lab tests.
